name: From Storage to Experience: A Survey on the Evolution of LLM Agent Memory Mechanisms (Luo et al.)
venue: ACL 2026 Findings (Accepted). First released as arXiv:2605.06716 [cs.AI] on 2026-05-07 (submitted 7 May 2026, v1). Subjects: cs.AI; cs.CL. The 'arXiv:2605.06716 (2026-05)' label refers to this same preprint; the peer-reviewed venue is ACL 2026 Findings.
authors_affiliation: Jinghao Luo (South China Normal University; equal contribution / project leader), Yuchen Tian (Hong Kong Baptist University; equal contribution), Chuxue Cao (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Ziyang Luo, Hongzhan Lin, Chuyi Kong (Hong Kong Baptist University), Kaixin Li (National University of Singapore), Ruichao Yang (University of Science and Technology Beijing), Jing Ma (Hong Kong Baptist University; corresponding author). Primary affiliation: Hong Kong Baptist University. Contact: FeishuEcho@outlook.com, {yctian, majing}@comp.hkbu.edu.hk.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/FeishuLuo/Evolving-LLM-Agent-Memory-Survey (continuously updated paper/resource list announced in the paper; README organized as Overview / Evolution Path / Paper List with Storage 33 papers, Reflection 28 papers, Experience 42 papers, and Benchmarks & Datasets 43 entries).
task_domain: Survey/taxonomy of memory mechanisms for LLM-based agents, spanning planning, tool-use, multi-step reasoning, long-context QA/dialogue, web navigation, embodied/open-world, code, recommendation/personalization, role-playing/social simulation, and multimodal/embodied settings (anchor evolutionary memory survey, not a single-task method).
problem_setting: A survey that reframes LLM-agent memory research, which it argues is fragmented between operating-system engineering and cognitive-science paradigms, into a single evolutionary perspective. It formalizes an LLM agent as a policy pi_theta(a_t | I, o_t, m_t) where m_t = Retrieve(M, o_t) is context-specific memory pulled from a global externalized repository M, and defines a trajectory tau = <(o_1,a_1),...,(o_T,a_T)>. It proposes a three-stage evolutionary framework (Storage -> Reflection -> Experience) based on the degree to which past interaction trajectories are utilized/abstracted. Settings covered are predominantly interactive, long-horizon, single- and multi-agent agent-environment loops; supervision varies by surveyed work. The survey proposes no new method, dataset, or experiments; it offers design principles and a roadmap. It explicitly notes that benchmarks for the Experience stage (abstraction/generalization) are scarce, and that current benchmarks mostly assess storage/retrieval of static data.
what_is_retrieved: Across surveyed systems: raw interaction trajectories / observation-action logs (Storage), refined/critiqued trajectory units and corrective insights (Reflection), and abstracted experiences -- natural-language heuristic guidelines/rules, reusable procedural skills/program functions, experience graphs, latent variables, and parameter-internalized priors (Experience). The survey frames retrieval as m_t = Retrieve(M, o_t): pulling context-specific memory from the global repository M for the current observation.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes is the central object (M is defined as an externalized repository bridging frozen parametric knowledge theta and evolving environmental dynamics, populated by Storage, Reflection, and Experience operations during interaction). It is HYBRID in that static external knowledge/long-context corpora and parametric/latent (internalized) memory are also covered, but the survey's organizing axis is the dynamically written, evolving trajectory store rather than a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Survey-level: storage/reflection-stage methods predominantly use similarity/weighted top-k retrieval (semantic proximity; relevance+recency+importance weighting a la Generative Agents; temporal-decay/Ebbinghaus weighting a la MemoryBank). A key argument is that the Experience stage transcends the top-k retrieval objective: abstracted rules/skills K act as a policy prior 'applicable to unseen scenarios without trajectory-level matching' (Table 1), and Experience compresses memory per the Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle (|K| << sum_tau |tau|). The survey does not advocate a single completeness-vs-top-k objective. [uncertain] as a single normative goal.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (a survey, not a CBR method). The three-stage workflow maps loosely onto a case lifecycle: Storage/Retrieve (preserve and recall trajectories), Reflection/Revise (critique, denoise, repair, dynamic maintenance), Experience/Retain+Reuse (abstract generalizable rules/skills reused as policy priors), but the survey does not use CBR Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain terminology.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False -- the survey frames memory via an evolutionary/cognitive lens (Storage->Reflection->Experience; statelessness, long-term consistency, dynamic environments, continual learning) and contrasts OS-engineering vs cognitive-science paradigms. It does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: Survey taxonomy of units rather than one: token/snippet (linear FIFO context streams), full/sub trajectories and observation-action logs (raw Storage), vector-encoded trajectory chunks (Vector storage), tabular rows / tiered-context entries / entity-relation triples and KG-subgraphs (Structured storage), refined memory units m'_i (Reflection), and abstracted experience units -- heuristic guidelines/rules, experience-graph nodes, reusable program functions/skills, latent token sequences, and internalized parameters (Experience). Defined by the degree of abstraction/cognitive processing.
index_source: Hybrid construction, but emphasizing online/test-time-induced growing memory: M is written during interaction (Storage appends raw trajectories M_raw = {tau_i}; Reflection injects refined units M <- M U {m'_i}; Experience extracts a separate rule set K). Storage also covers static long-context handling, and Experience covers offline-induced parameter internalization. The survey contrasts static-storage paradigms with active-management and abstraction paradigms.
index_structure_topology: Survey spans multiple topologies, explicitly enumerated in the Storage taxonomy: Linear (chronological token stream, FIFO; context-window adaptation + information sparsification), Vector (flat high-dimensional embedding index; semantic + weighted retrieval), and Structured (tabular relational databases e.g. ChatDB/DB-GPT/MAC-SQL; tiered/hierarchical architectures e.g. MemGPT/MemoChat/MemOS; and semantic/entity-relation GRAPHS e.g. MemLLM/AriGraph/GraphReader). No single topology prescribed.
retriever_type: Survey-level / hybrid across works: dense semantic retrieval (embedding proximity), weighted retrieval (relevance+recency+importance, temporal decay), BM25/lexical and visual channels (in multimodal parallel-fusion), LLM/SQL-generated structured queries (ChatDB/DB-GPT), graph traversal (semantic graphs), agent-driven/autonomous retrieval controllers, and -- in implicit/hybrid Experience -- parameter-/latent-based 'reading' via forward pass (no explicit retriever). No canonical retriever proposed.
retriever_learning_signal: Survey-level: storage/reflection-stage reading is predominantly off-the-shelf (text similarity, heuristic relevance/recency/importance, temporal-decay weighting). The survey highlights a shift toward learned/RL-optimized signals chiefly in the Experience stage (RL on reflections, group-based policy optimization, RL-aligned tool invocation, early-experience/implicit-world-model paradigms, soft-Q / value-style internalization) and toward agent-learned retrieval controllers (active memory perception). It proposes no retriever itself; learning signals discussed range from none (similarity) to environment-feedback and RL.
query_construction: Survey-level: queries to memory are formed from the current observation/state (m_t = Retrieve(M, o_t)); via agent-generated structured queries (LLM-to-SQL in ChatDB/DB-GPT); via query-key similarity over memory blocks; via multi-channel queries (semantic/lexical/visual) in multimodal retrieval; and via agent-driven multi-turn intent-conditioned queries. Construction is method-dependent; abstracted as observation-conditioned memory reading.
query_granularity: Survey-level: predominantly step/state-level reading (memory retrieved per observation o_t during reasoning/acting), with task-level/session-level reads also present and, in the Experience stage, abstracted rules used as priors without trajectory-level matching. The survey does not standardize a query granularity.
when_to_retrieve: Survey-level: both one-shot and iterative reading appear; an explicit future direction ('Active Memory Perception') argues for adaptive, learned/autonomous triggering -- agents should evaluate on-demand whether and what type of memory is needed -- moving beyond passive, indiscriminate retrieval. Some surveyed systems already use autonomous retrieval controllers; no single trigger policy is prescribed.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Survey-level: triggers across works include fixed schedule (read per step/turn), similarity/weighted thresholds, agent-initiated/self-directed access (MemGPT-style OS controllers; LLM-generated SQL reads), and -- as a flagged future direction -- learned autonomous retrieval controllers that decide whether/what memory to introduce on demand. The survey critiques passive triggering and indiscriminate retrieval (irrelevant/obsolete memories disrupt reasoning coherence). No token-confidence/attention trigger is adopted as a unifying signal.
reranking: Survey-level: not a central focus. Weighted retrieval (combining relevance, recency, importance; temporal/Ebbinghaus decay) functions as a scoring/prioritization stage, and multimodal 'parallel fusion' uses rank fusion across semantic/lexical/visual channels and 'hierarchical retrieval' cascades coarse-to-fine. No dedicated cross-encoder reranker is prescribed. [uncertain] as a standardized stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: Survey-level: refinement is a defining axis. Storage uses information sparsification / compression (attention-score eviction H2O, query-key salient-block retrieval Quest, perplexity-based redundancy removal LLMLingua). Reflection performs semantic refinement: error rectification (self-critique/repair), dynamic maintenance (lifecycle update/dedup), and knowledge compression/distillation (structured reflections, modular procedural decomposition, multi-granularity abstraction, context-folding e.g. AgentFold). Experience performs cross-trajectory abstraction/induction. So: rerank/decompose-then-recompose/distill/compress/filter all appear, organized by stage.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (memory survey; tool/skill-description indexing engineering is largely out of scope, though procedural-skill libraries and tool-use experience internalization are discussed in the Experience stage).
index_content_separation: Partially covered: tiered/hierarchical storage architectures (e.g., MemGPT dual-layer main vs external context with virtual context expansion; MemoChat topic-keyed segments; MemOS) separate a small in-context working memory from a larger external store paged/retrieved on demand; SWIFT-SAGE dynamically adjusts retrieval intensity. Discussed as a storage-management pattern rather than a formal lightweight-index-then-content principle.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index / integration protocol such as RapidAPI/MCP; memory stores grow via in-loop trajectory writing and OS-style controller updates rather than tool-API CRUD sync).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (inter-tool dependency modeling is out of scope; the survey's structured/graph storage models entity-relation dependencies of the environment, and Experience models causal/cross-step dependencies, but not tool-to-tool dependency graphs).
how_retrieved_used: Survey-level: retrieved memory is used as prompt/context augmentation (injecting recalled trajectories/insights into pi_theta(a_t | I, o_t, m_t)); as refined references for similar future tasks (Reflection units m'_i); as reusable skills/program functions invoked as atomic actions and natural-language heuristic guidelines/rules used as policy priors for unseen tasks (explicit Experience); as latent token injection / activation modulation (latent Experience, e.g., MemGen 'Memory Weaver'); and as a training signal -- internalizing experience into model parameters via fine-tuning/RL (implicit and hybrid Experience).
planning_integration: Survey-level: memory supports planning/acting by supplying past observations/experiences at decision time (per-step interleaved retrieval m_t = Retrieve(M, o_t)); by providing persistent high-level goals to prevent goal drift in long-horizon and multi-agent planning; by guiding active exploration (reward/curriculum/reuse-driven) whose outcomes are abstracted back into memory; and -- in Experience -- by elevating pi_theta to decision-making at a higher level of abstraction via rule/skill priors that enable zero-shot transfer to unseen scenarios. The survey abstracts integration as a Storage->Reflection->Experience evolution rather than prescribing one plan-time scheme.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Survey-level: reviewed works interleave memory reading at per-step / per-turn granularity during reasoning and acting (m_t per observation o_t), with per-answer/session reads also present and Experience priors applied without per-step trajectory matching. The survey does not impose a single interleaving granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (a survey, not a CBR adaptation method). The closest analogues it surveys are Reflection's revision/refinement (self-critique error rectification, dynamic maintenance, distillation) and Experience's adaptation/reuse (LLM-prompted heuristic-rule reuse, skill composition/cascading, RL/fine-tuning internalization, latent modulation).
retrieved_item_representation: Survey-level spectrum tied to the three stages: (Storage) raw trajectory token streams, vector embeddings, tabular rows, tiered-context entries, entity-relation graphs; (Reflection) distilled/critiqued free-text memory units m'_i, structured profiles, compressed procedural memories, folded context; (Experience) human-readable natural-language guidelines/rules, experience graphs, executable program functions/skills, latent/soft token sequences (MemGen), and internalized model parameters. Surface forms thus range from raw trajectory to distilled rule to executable skill to latent/parametric.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Survey-level the central axis: classification is explicitly by 'degree of utilization/abstraction of past trajectories.' Storage = raw trajectory fidelity (one-to-one with execution traces); Reflection = intra-trajectory refined units (quality density, context-tied); Experience = inter-trajectory inductive abstraction into universal rules/skills K detached from any specific scenario (policy prior). Experience abstraction is further graded shallow (NL rules) -> intermediate (modular executable skeletons/skills) -> deep (parameter-internalized intuition).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Survey-level: a core motivation. Reflection is the principal robustness mechanism -- it acts as a 'semantic filter' against hallucinations/logic errors/invalid attempts via introspective self-critique (error rectification, post-reasoning verification, consistency checks), environmental feedback grounding, and coordinative/consensus calibration. Storage uses sparsification/denoising; Experience uses contrastive induction over success/failure trajectories to sharpen policy boundaries and abstraction to avoid context-shift errors from following raw successful trajectories. Active Memory Perception (future) targets filtering irrelevant/obsolete retrievals.
memory_type: Survey/taxonomy -- covers all listed types organized by the Storage/Reflection/Experience evolution: linear/episodic context streams, vector memory, structured (tabular/tiered/graph) memory, skill-library and workflow/procedural memory (explicit Experience), and latent/parametric memory (implicit Experience: latent modulation, parameter internalization). It does not pick one.
write_back: True (survey-level) -- writing to M is foundational: Storage appends raw trajectories (M_raw = {tau_i}_{i=1}^N), Reflection injects refined units (M <- M U {m'_i}), and Experience extracts/accumulates an abstracted rule/skill set K (and, in hybrid, internalizes it into parameters). Write-back is described as central across stages, not a single implementation.
online_growth: Yes (survey-level) -- M grows during interaction across all three stages; a key continual-learning driver is that long-horizon real-world interaction causes linear memory expansion, and the survey explicitly warns that unrestricted growth degrades performance (errors propagate and contaminate learning), motivating strategic add/delete policies, decay, pruning, and abstraction-based compression.
write_back_trigger: Survey-level: triggers vary by stage/work -- per-step/turn appending (Storage); reflective writing after a completed trajectory (m'_i = F_ref(tau_i | phi); Reflexion-style post-trial reflection); on-success-and-failure storage for contrastive abstraction (Experience); OS-controller / lifecycle-managed updates (MemGPT/Mem0/Zep dynamic maintenance); and periodic parameter-update internalization (hybrid Accumulate-Internalize cycle). No single trigger prescribed; the survey advocates more strategic, possibly learned, add/delete policies.
failure_experience_usage: Survey-level: explicitly important. Reflexion-style Reflection distills corrective feedback from FAILED trajectories into textual memory; the Experience stage uses contrastive induction over successful AND failed trajectories to delineate policy boundaries precisely (Forouzandeh et al. 2025; He et al. 2024c). The survey also cautions that agents over-follow successful trajectories, and that corrected-but-unabstracted trajectories still induce errors under context shift -- motivating abstraction. Thus success+failure contrastive usage is a recognized mechanism.
memory_evolution_update: Survey-level: stored entries are mutated beyond append-only. Reflection performs delta-update/refine-overwrite (error rectification, repair, consistency-based deletion) and dynamic maintenance (incremental schema update via clustering, entity-relation parsing/update, OS-controller persist/evict). Storage uses forget/prune (FIFO eviction, attention/perplexity-based token eviction, temporal decay). Experience performs dedup-merge and compression (cross-trajectory induction satisfying MDL) and link-and-evolve (experience graphs) plus internalization into parameters. So append-only / dedup-merge / delta-update / refine-overwrite / forget-prune / link-and-evolve all appear.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Survey-level: storage/reflection retrieval is predominantly fixed similarity/weighted top-k (not a learned policy). However, the survey foregrounds a shift toward learned/RL-optimized policies in the Experience stage and in retrieval control: RL on reflections, group-based policy optimization, RL-aligned tool invocation, early-experience/implicit-world-model internalization, and 'Active Memory Perception' autonomous retrieval controllers. It proposes no learned policy itself but documents the trend from fixed top-k to learned policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes, covered as a recognized and future-emphasized axis: Coordination/Collaborative reflection builds societies of heterogeneous agents using role division and consensus (CSR, CoGent, MIRIX); shared goal memory turns isolated behaviors into coordinated collective execution in multi-agent systems; and 'Distributed Shared Memory' is a headline future direction -- arguing current dialogue-based sharing is bandwidth-limited/noisy and advocating consensus memory systems for socialized experience evolution. So cross-agent/shared memory is both surveyed and flagged as a key open problem.
benchmarks: No new benchmark is introduced. The survey catalogs 43 representative datasets/benchmarks (Tables 2-3) grouped by stage. Storage stage: LongBench, LongBench v2, RULER, MMNeedle, HotpotQA, MemoryBank, BABILong, DialSim, LongMemEval, BEAM, MPR, LOCCO, MADial-Bench, HELMET. Reflection stage: Minerva, HaluMem, MABench, PRM, PersonMem v2, LoCoMo, WebChoreArena, MT-Mind2Web, StoryBench, PerLTQA, ImplexConv, Share, Mem-PAL, PrefEval, LIDB. Experience stage: StreamBench, MemoryBench, Evo-Memory, LABench. It notes Experience-stage benchmarks are scarce.
benchmark_family: memory (agent-memory evaluation survey). Sub-families spanned: extreme-context / long-context (RULER, BABILong, HELMET, LongBench/v2, MMNeedle-multimodal), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, MPR), long-term/cross-session dialogue & persona consistency (MemoryBank, DialSim, LongMemEval, BEAM, LOCCO, LoCoMo, MADial-Bench), memory-hallucination/lifecycle (Minerva, HaluMem, MABench), personalization (PRM, PersonMem v2, PerLTQA, ImplexConv, Share, Mem-PAL, PrefEval, LIDB), web/embodied dynamic reasoning (WebChoreArena, MT-Mind2Web, StoryBench), and continual/lifelong/test-time experience learning (StreamBench, MemoryBench, Evo-Memory, LABench).
baselines: N/A -- a survey with no experiments. Instead of baselines it organizes and compares representative systems by stage in Figure 4's taxonomy, e.g.: Storage -- PCW, StreamingLLM, SelfExtend, H2O, Quest, LLMLingua (Linear); ARMRAG, MemLong, Larimar, MemoryBank, Stanford Generative Agents (Vector); ChatDB, DB-GPT, MAC-SQL, MemGPT, MemoChat, MemOS, MemLLM, AriGraph, GraphReader (Structured). Reflection -- Reflexion, TiM, LLM-MapRepair, Zep, Mem0, CAMA, MemOrb, LEGOMem, AgentFold, DEAL, ToolMem, CLIN, Memory-R1, MDSF, Self-Goal, MIRIX, CoGent, CSR. Experience -- FLEX, ArcMem, LightMem, CASCADE, IPS, AccelOpt (Explicit); MemGen, LatentEvolve, AgentEvolver, Agent-LV, Verl (Implicit); ReasoningBank, EvolveR, Hybrid-Replay (Hybrid).
key_metrics: Survey-level: no metrics computed. It discusses, per benchmark, metrics such as QA accuracy / answer correctness, multi-needle retrieval accuracy, multi-hop reasoning accuracy, retrieval precision/recall, persona/relationship consistency, memory fidelity (fabrication/omission rates as in HaluMem), test-time/continual-learning improvement and knowledge-transfer/generalization (StreamBench, Evo-Memory, LABench), and information-decay measures. It also conceptually distinguishes memory capacity vs reasoning precision.
headline_result: N/A (no empirical headline number; it is a survey). Its headline contribution is the evolutionary three-stage framework -- Storage (trajectory preservation), Reflection (trajectory refinement), Experience (trajectory abstraction) -- formalized as F_ref: T->S (intra-trajectory transformation m'_i = F_ref(tau_i | phi)) vs F_exp: T_batch -> K (inter-trajectory induction with |K| << sum |tau|, an MDL-style compression to a policy prior), plus the two transformative Experience mechanisms (active exploration, cross-trajectory abstraction). 216 references; 6 citations (Semantic Scholar, as of mid-2026).
ablations: N/A (no experiments/ablations). The closest analytical artifact is Table 1, a structural comparison between Reflection and Experience along functional signature, output form (refined unit m'_i tied to task context vs universal rules/skills K detached from any scenario), retrieval dependency (similar-task retrieval at inference vs policy prior for unseen scenarios without trajectory matching), and representative works (Reflexion/CLIN/AgentFold vs FLEX/MemSkill/SkillRL).
evaluation_decoupling: Survey-level: implicitly via the stage-structured benchmark taxonomy -- Storage benchmarks isolate intrinsic storage/retrieval (multi-needle, retrieval precision) while Reflection/Experience benchmarks target denoising fidelity and abstraction/generalization/continual learning. The survey argues most current benchmarks over-assess static storage/retrieval and under-assess Experience-stage abstraction, calling for benchmarks that decouple and target meta-learning/generalization. It does not standardize separate intrinsic-vs-end-to-end reporting (Recall@k vs task success) itself. [uncertain] as a formal protocol.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Survey-level: advocates measuring more than final outcome. It distinguishes capacity for accurate storage/retrieval, memory fidelity (process-level fabrication/omission, e.g., HaluMem/Minerva over the memory lifecycle), dynamic-reasoning/backtracking quality, and abstraction/generalization/transfer (Experience). The framing pushes toward process- and lifecycle-level memory evaluation, not just end-task success, but the survey itself reports no scores.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively as a primary driver: context-window/storage constraints and the cost of unrestricted memory growth (retrieval latency, inference burden, error propagation). Storage trades capacity vs retrieval speed (tiered architectures); Experience explicitly compresses memory (MDL: |K| << sum_tau |tau|) to cut retrieval/inference overhead and enable zero-shot transfer; implicit/hybrid Experience internalizes experience into parameters to remove retrieval dependence ('Storage Explosion' and 'Retrieval Latency' mitigation). No concrete latency/cost numbers (it is a survey).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Survey-level: the limited context window vs expanding interaction history is the foundational Storage motivation. Methods manage budget via FIFO eviction, context-window extension (PCW/StreamingLLM/SelfExtend), sparsification/compression (H2O/Quest/LLMLingua), tiered/virtual context (MemGPT), context-folding (AgentFold), and Experience-stage compression into compact rules/skills/parameters. Reads are typically fixed/weighted top-k. No single budget/k value is prescribed.
survey_scope_and_axes: Organizing logic is 'Why-How-What' over a dynamic-evolution framework. Axes: (Why / Evolutionary Drivers) Long-Term Consistency {state, goals}, Dynamic Environments {temporal validity of knowledge, causal structure}, Continual Learning {storage constraints, requirement for experience}; (How / Evolutionary Path) Storage {Linear: context-window adaptation, information sparsification; Vector: semantic retrieval, weighted retrieval; Structured: tabular database, tiered architectures, semantic graphs} -> Reflection {Introspection: error rectification, dynamic maintenance, knowledge compression; Environment: environment modeling, decision optimization; Coordination: multi-dimensional calibration} -> Experience {Explicit: heuristic guidelines, procedural primitives; Implicit: latent modulation, parameter internalization; Hybrid: experience transfer}; (What / Transformative Experience) Active Exploration {mechanisms: reward/curriculum/reuse-driven; dimensions: breadth/depth/strategy} and Cross-Trajectory Abstraction {mechanisms: contrastive induction, multi-granularity chunking, code encapsulation, parameter internalization; granularity: shallow NL rules / intermediate executable skeletons / deep parametric}. Future Directions: active memory perception, working-memory organization, Experience benchmarks, distributed shared memory, multimodal memory (Appendix C). 216 references; coverage through 2025 (claimed first evolution-perspective memory survey), with 2026-dated frontier works.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (proposes no benchmark). It tabulates 43 existing datasets with sizes/construction in Tables 2-3, e.g. LongBench (4.7k, up to 32k tokens), LongBench v2 (503, 8k-2M words), RULER (scalable, multi-needle/multi-hop), BABILong (scalable, up to 1M tokens), HELMET (scalable, up to 128k tokens), HotpotQA (113k, multi-hop Wikipedia), MMNeedle (280k, multimodal), MemoryBank (194, 10-day dialogue), LoCoMo (50, 35 sessions), LongMemEval (500), HaluMem (3.5k, fabrication/omission), StreamBench (9.7k, online learning), MemoryBench (20k, continual learning), Evo-Memory (3.7k, test-time learning), LABench (1.4k, lifelong learning). It notes current benchmarks mostly assess static storage/retrieval and that Experience-stage benchmarks are scarce.
builds_on: Prior LLM-agent memory surveys it extends/critiques -- Zhang et al. 2024 (engineering-module classification of agent memory) and Hu et al. 2025 (dynamic memory processes); cognitive-architecture framing (Sumers et al. CoALA). Foundational memory/agent systems it taxonomizes: ReAct, Reflexion, Generative Agents (Stanford Town), MemGPT, MemoryBank, ChatDB, TiM, MemoChat, MemOS, AriGraph, GraphReader, Mem0, Zep, CLIN; and frontier Experience works ReasoningBank, EvolveR, AgentEvolver, MemGen, LatentEvolve, FLEX. Theoretical grounding: Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle for the Experience-stage compression operator.
contrasts_with: Positions itself against prior agent-memory surveys (Zhang et al. 2024; Hu et al. 2025; Wu et al. 2025; Du et al. 2025; Wu & Shu 2025; Cao et al. 2025) that organize memory by static functional/engineering categories and lack a unified evolutionary perspective, thereby obscuring the technical drivers of memory development. It also contrasts the two fragmented paradigms it seeks to unify -- OS-engineering memory management vs cognitive-science memory simulation -- and internally contrasts Storage vs Reflection vs Experience (Table 1: intra-trajectory refinement vs inter-trajectory abstraction).
lineage: Surveys group -- an evolution-perspective memory survey for LLM-based agents (Storage -> Reflection -> Experience). It sits downstream of foundational agent-memory surveys (e.g., Zhang et al. 2024 'A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of LLM-based Agents') and is a sibling of contemporaneous 2025-2026 memory/experience surveys; it directly anchors the experiential-agent lineage by linking ExpeL/Reflexion/AWM-style works to its taxonomy (Reflexion in Reflection; ReasoningBank/skill-induction/AWM-style procedural primitives and cross-trajectory abstraction in Experience), formalizing the shift from trajectory storage to policy-prior abstraction.
